bundles.name: The turn loop: four steps that do nothing (and one that does everything twice)
items: #4 PARTIAL — Power-Up applies twice per turn. packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:92 runs powerUp() on step entry without setting state.poweredUpThisTurn; the guard at reducer.ts:105-114 therefore lets one more full power-up through, and packages/client/src/components/Board.tsx:207 enables exactly that button in exactly that step. MP climbs 2x PUR, Allies climb 2 stages instead of 1. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

#2 OPEN — Discard Step is a pass-through. No hand limit exists anywhere: reducer.ts:90-93 has no 'discard' branch and a repo-wide grep for handLimit/HAND_LIMIT/'all but 1' across engine, shared and server returns nothing. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS. Needs a prompt (CRD 240-241: attacker discards to 1, then opponent does the same).

#5 OPEN — Declare Step is not a decision. turn.ts:47-48/65 walks declare -> combat unconditionally; the only bypass is turn.ts:59 keyed on skipCombatThisTurn, written solely at noncombat.ts:83. No declareCombat action exists in packages/shared/src/protocol.ts:9-31. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

#25 OPEN — Rejuvenation Step is a pass-through. No 'rejuvenation' branch in reducer.ts:90-93; rejuvenate() at abilities.ts:151-162 is correct but reachable only as a card effect. Its precondition (did not declare Combat) is unrepresentable until #5 lands, though the Location/Battleground path is already recordable today.
bundles.whyItMatters: This is the only bundle that fires every single turn for both players regardless of deck, and three of its four items are complete no-ops. Hands grow without bound (3 cards a Draw Step plus 3 more in every Prepare Phase, never trimmed), so a defence card is always in hand and attacks rarely land; personalities sit at the top of their ladder every turn, which inflates every PAT lookup and neuters attrition; and the attacker can never decline Combat, so the defender is handed 3 free cards every turn and the whole defensive/rebuild line of play does not exist.
bundles.unlocks: Card economy becomes a real constraint, which is the precondition for every combat fix downstream mattering. Declining Combat makes the Rejuvenation entitlement reachable and gives Locations/Battlegrounds their intended payoff. Correct power stages make the PAT numbers in bundle 2 meaningful.
bundles.approach: Do the one-line power-up fix first (set state.poweredUpThisTurn in reducer.ts:92) — ten minutes, and it corrects every PAT bracket in the game. Then add declaredCombat to GameState + a declareCombat action, widen the turn.ts:59 redirect, and build the discard and rejuvenation prompts on the existing pendingPrompt machinery. Migration cost: the fast-forward loops in engine.test.ts:85/99/134 spin `while (step !== 'combat') advanceStep` and will hang unless a declareCombat is injected.

bundles.name: Attack declaration: source, cost, and when the PAT is read
items: #3 OPEN — an attack can be declared with no card, no power and no cost, unlimited times. combat.ts:214-234 validates a card only `if (cardUid)`; nothing is spent (the spend helper opens `if (!uid) return;` at combat.ts:478-479); Board.tsx:194-195 ships two bare buttons that send no cardUid. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

#7 OPEN — the energy attack's 2-stage cost is not enforced. combat.ts:258-263 discards loseStages' unpayable remainder and there is no affordability guard, so an attacker at stageIndex 0 attacks free forever. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

#9 OPEN — Physical Base Damage is computed at declaration (combat.ts:266-268) from the pre-announcement controller, before openControlWindow at combat.ts:277; resolveControlOfCombat writes only defenderControllerUid at combat.ts:348 and never recomputes. Naming a healthy Ally moves the damage but keeps the crushed MP's PAT number. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

#30 OPEN — Final Physical Attack unreachable. finalUsed is initialised (combat.ts:86) and guarded twice (combat.ts:228, :601) but never written; no action exists in protocol.ts. Land it with #3: the cardless attack is currently the illegitimate substitute for it.
#34 OPEN — double/triple base damage parses silently with no needsReview flag and no multiplier term in the combat.ts:722 total (8 cards). Small, and it belongs in the same arithmetic.
bundles.whyItMatters: Every attack in every game passes through here. Today the dominant line is 'press Physical attack, spend nothing, keep your whole hand for defence' — deck construction and card economy stop mattering on the offensive side exactly as they do on the hand-size side. The base-damage timing bug is worse than it looks: the control window only opens when the defender's MP is at its bottom two stages, i.e. precisely when the PAT gap is widest, so a defender is punished for using the rule correctly and the excess overflows into life cards that can cross the 5-card capture threshold.
bundles.unlocks: Combat cards become a spent resource; Control of Combat becomes worth using; Final Physical Attack (the desperation line that closes games) becomes playable with its real cost and lockout.
bundles.approach: Requiring a real attack source is the expensive part — 58 of 63 declareAttack call sites across the engine tests pass `undefined` as cardUid, so build a shared fixture helper that instantiates a stock Physical Combat card first. Move the computeBaseDamage call out of declareAttack into resolveDefense just above the combat.ts:722 total, re-reading both controllers (the attacker's rating can move too, abilities.ts:123-124), and keep a distinct flag for 'the card stated a fixed base' rather than overloading `baseDamage === undefined`.

bundles.name: Defence resolution: what a card played as a defence actually does
items: #0 PARTIAL — the residue. combat.ts:638-658 still falls through to `atk.stopped = true` for any card the parser produced no ability for, with the attack-type match at combat.ts:631-637 never run (it sits inside the `stops.length > 0` branch). 442 combat-typed cards in data/cards.tts.enriched.json carry no parsed ability, 284 of them printing attack text. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS. Widen the scope: the refutation found the same path also upgrades a prevention-only defence (trigger 'defense', no stopAttack) to a full type-agnostic stop, which a text-based predicate would not catch. defenseEffects (combat.ts:907-915) also still hands attack-trigger effects to the defensive rider path.

#10 OPEN — preventLifeCards has no consumer anywhere (emitted abilities.ts:452-453, typed shared/abilities.ts:50, read by nothing), so a prevent-N card cancels the attack outright, and because atk.stopped is set the attack is never successful — the attacker also loses the capture and every if-successful rider. CRD:340: an attack is successful even if it deals no damage.

#11 OPEN — combat.ts:660-662 grants a combat-long lockout on any thisCombat stop without reading e.scope, so a one-shot Defense Shield ('stops the FIRST unstopped physical attack this Combat') ends the opponent's entire offense for the Combat Step. ~17-18 cards.

#44 OPEN — that lockout is enforced at declaration (combat.ts:229-230), above setupAttackAbility, above the cost, above any spend. So secondary effects never resolve (CRD:387), 'if this attack is stopped' riders can never fire, the card is never spent, and cards printed as exceptions to a lockout (Orange Energy Discharge) are unplayable.

#29 OPEN — deferred stops ('next phase', 'first successful') are filtered out at combat.ts:631 and the card is refused at every moment, so 9 cards are dead in hand. The parser also collapses 'stops X and stops X next phase' into a single deferred stop (abilities.ts:433 claims the whole sentence).

#26 OPEN — Focused is stripped at abilities.ts:672-673 and used only for a needsReview note; no Effect or AttackInProgress field carries it, so the coverage test at combat.ts:632 lets a dual-type stop block the 62 cards printed to beat exactly that.
bundles.whyItMatters: The single most-used decision in combat. Roughly a third of the combat pool is still a universal 'stop anything' regardless of printed type, prevention cards nullify attacks instead of reducing them, and one Defense Shield can shut down a whole Combat Step. Net effect: attacks land far less often than the rules allow, and when a defence does fire, the wrong thing happens on both sides of it.
bundles.unlocks: Attacks start landing at their real rate, which is what makes bundles 2 and 4 visible at the table. It also introduces the stop-vs-prevent distinction (CRD:306-307) that Endurance, Focused and the Dragon Ball threshold all depend on.
bundles.approach: One sitting in resolveDefense. Add lifeCardPrevention to AttackInProgress and let a prevention-only card fall through to steps 7/8 instead of returning early; make defenseEffects return [] rather than falling back to attack-trigger abilities; run the type-match on the no-modelled-stop path using the printed type; guard the lockout write with `e.scope === 'all'`; move the lockout check from declaration into resolution as a stop applied to a performed attack. #29 needs a pendingStops registry on CombatState plus a parser split on ' and '. Note defence-economy.test.ts:132-140 deliberately locks the current pass-through in and will need rewriting.

bundles.name: Damage arithmetic: the terms that never get added
items: #6 OPEN — no code path anywhere reads either player's zones.inPlay to modify damage. combat.ts:722 is a pure sum of card-local terms, atk.modifiers is written only from the attack card (abilities.ts:113), and the 'constant' trigger (shared/abilities.ts:14) is executed by nothing. 85 Drills print a signed damage clause and every one is inert in both directions.

#22 OPEN — '+N life cards of damage' is parsed to a bare flag (abilities.ts:377-383) with no Effect kind to carry it and no term in either damage path. 51 abilities lose the life-card half of their printed damage.

#23 OPEN — an attack stating both life cards and power stages deals only one of the two, in opposite directions for physical and energy (abilities.ts:103-110 plus the early return at combat.ts:701-716). The parser was fixed; the executor still throws one half away.

#39 OPEN — changeControllerStages clamps at 0 (abilities.ts:47-48) and drops the remainder, so a card-effect drain below zero discards no life cards (CRD:390). discardForEffect exists at damage.ts:89 with no production caller. 13 abilities affected, 6 of them on cards that do not say 'to a minimum of 0'.
bundles.whyItMatters: With the real PAT loaded (data/pat.json, placeholder:false), Drill modifiers are frequently the largest single term in a physical attack, and nearly every deck runs Drills — so physical damage totals are wrong in essentially every game. The other three are silent partial resolutions: the card does something, just not the printed amount, so players will not notice they are being cheated.
bundles.unlocks: Damage numbers you can trust, which is also what makes the 5-life-card Dragon Ball capture threshold and Survival pacing correct.
bundles.approach: #6 is the large one and drives the shape: it needs qualifiers on damageStages ('yoursOnly' vs 'againstYou', attack type), new parser rules for the two printed shapes, a data re-bake, and a boardModifiers(state, ...) helper consulted at combat.ts:714 and :722 with a floor at 0. #22/#23/#39 are each an Effect-union addition plus a couple of executor lines and ride along cheaply once the plumbing is open.

bundles.name: Server authority, input validation and prompt identity
items: authorize() only rejects a NUMERIC playerIdx — packages/server/src/room.ts:280 `typeof named === 'number' && named !== seatIdx`, so `playerIdx: '1'` skips the check and JS array indexing resolves the string anyway. Verified exploits: drawCards for the opponent empties their Life Deck for an instant Survival win; concede with a spoofed idx makes the sender the winner; chat impersonates the opponent in the shared log. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS (the guard reads exactly as reported).

moveCard validates neither toZone nor toPlayerIdx — reducer.ts:166 `state.players[action.toPlayerIdx ?? loc.playerIdx]!.zones[action.toZone].push(inst)`. An unknown zone or out-of-range seat throws an uncaught TypeError that propagates through room.ts:179 and the bare ws listener at index.ts:71, killing the whole process and every game in it. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

moveCard also reads and steals from zones the sender does not own — findInstance walks both players' zones, redact.ts:12 preserves the real uid on hidden cards, so one message at a time reveals the opponent's hand and Life Deck, and a loop over their deck ends the game by Survival. The room.ts:273-277 tabletop-assist exemption is about touching an opponent's card, not about defeating redaction.

answerPrompt ignores action.promptId — reducer.ts:195-217 dispatches purely on state.pendingPrompt?.type. Because one action can close a prompt and open the next for the same player (resolveDefense -> resolveLifeCardDamage opens the endurance prompt at combat.ts:777), a double-clicked button silently spends the defender's Endurance card and forfeits the prevention. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS (promptId appears nowhere in engine or server).

drawCards has no step, turn or count validation — reducer.ts:96 `draw(state, action.playerIdx, action.count)`. A player can draw 20 cards for their own seat during the opponent's turn, and authorize() passes it because the seat matches.

setStage accepts a non-numeric stageIndex — turn.ts:149 Math.max(0, Math.min('x', n)) yields NaN, giving stageIndex NaN and currentRating undefined, which poisons every later PAT lookup, makes `stageIndex > MP_DOWN_STAGES` permanently false, and cannot be recovered by normal play. (The cross-seat targeting half is a documented deliberate exemption — fix only the type guard.)

Dragon Ball capture is not gated on a pending capture prompt — combat.ts:870-872 checks only that an attack exists and the caller is the attacker; no `pendingPrompt?.type === 'capture'` check and no lifeCardsDealt >= 5 check, unlike every sibling resolver. The call also deletes the defender's open prompt and cancels the in-flight attack. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.
chat text is unbounded and state.log is never trimmed (reducer.ts:227), and room.ts:243-265 re-serialises the whole log to every client on every action.

senseiCardId survives the redaction that hides zones.sensei (redact.ts:29 vs the `{...p, zones}` spread at :33). Per CRD:88 the Sensei card is public, so delete the dead hiding rather than redacting the field.
bundles.whyItMatters: Honest frequency note: two friends will not send hand-crafted WebSocket messages, so most of this bundle is near-zero frequency at the table. It is ranked here anyway because the promptId bug is hit by an ordinary double-click and silently destroys a defender's Endurance decision, the moveCard crash takes down every game in the process, and every item is individually a few lines. Severity per unit of effort is the highest in the worklist.
bundles.unlocks: The server can be exposed beyond a fully trusted LAN, and prompt answers stop being ambiguous — which matters more as bundles 1-3 add more prompts (discard, rejuvenation, declare, prevention).
bundles.approach: Almost all one-liners: reject any playerIdx that is not a number equal to seatIdx; validate toZone against the ZONES tuple and toPlayerIdx against range; Number.isInteger on stageIndex; compare action.promptId to state.pendingPrompt.id; gate resolveCapture on the capture prompt; cap chat text; delete the sensei hiding. The uid-adjacency leak (identical cards get consecutive uids because buildLifeDeck creates all copies in one run before shuffling, setup.ts:59-65) is fixed by stamping uids after the shuffle.

bundles.name: Anger arithmetic and personality levels
items: #14 OPEN — conditional 'instead' clauses are additive. pushAnger (abilities.ts:500-544) pushes one changeAnger per clause with no reference to CONDITIONAL_CLAUSE (declared abilities.ts:299, used only inside parseAttackDamage). Shipped data confirms it: Black Hug Maneuver [+2,+3] = a free personality level off one attack; Gohan's Temper, Empowerment!, Goku's Super Saiyan Catch all +3 instead of 1; Orange Thumbs Up strips 3 instead of 1. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS (the loop and the terminal push read exactly as reported).

#15 OPEN — prohibition clauses are executed as anger changes. pushAnger has no negation test at all, and toNum's fallback of 1 supplies a phantom +1. Awful Abrasions / Severe Bruises / Terrible Wounds / Goku's Heart Disease zero the victim's anger then hand back +1; Blue Head Charge's 'your opponent cannot gain any anger' mis-targets as +1 to the ATTACKER; Red Commander nets 0; Goku's Farewell nets -4. The refutation pass found 30 such cards in the catalog, not the 7 the finding names.

#47 OPEN (latent) — advanceLevel wipes anger unconditionally at turn.ts:165 even when the advance was not by 5 anger (CRD:526). One line, and it goes live the moment #24 or any card-effect advance lands.

#24 OPEN — losing a personality level is not implemented at all: nothing decrements currentLevel anywhere, there is no Effect kind for it, and the affected cards fail silently (Roshi's/King Kai's Calming parse to no ability and sit inert with no 'resolve manually' notice; Majin Buu's Bicycle Kick's clause is swallowed as a delta-0 changeAnger that counts as resolved).
bundles.whyItMatters: 5 anger advances a personality level and reaching the top level by anger is the Most Powerful Personality victory — so the game's fastest win condition currently arrives roughly twice as fast as printed, and the cards printed to shut anger down feed it instead. Anger cards are common enough that a typical game hits several of these.
bundles.unlocks: A believable clock on the MPPV race, and the printed counterplay against a runaway anger deck.
bundles.approach: #14/#15/#47 are one sitting: a CONDITIONAL_CLAUSE skip and a negation guard inside pushAnger's per-clause loop (both must sit before the toZero branch at abilities.ts:528 so the legitimate 'lower to 0' half survives), a needsReview flag plumbed out to all three parseAbility call sites, one line at turn.ts:165, then re-bake data/cards.tts.enriched.json and data/cards.saiyan.enriched.json via enrich-tts.ts:472 and author.ts:37. #24 is a separate, larger piece (new Effect kind, loseLevel in turn.ts, Drill discard per CRD:636, anger deliberately untouched per CRD:526) — split it out if the sitting runs long.

bundles.name: Allies and Control of Combat
items: #16 OPEN — a level-2+ Ally collapses to power rating 0. reducer.ts:151-152 builds it with `levelCardIds: [inst.cardId]` but `currentLevel: per.level`, and currentRatings (turn.ts:88) reads `levelCardIds[currentLevel - 1]` -> undefined -> `?? [0]`. The Ally enters looking correct at 3 stages above 0 and is destroyed by its owner's very next Power-Up Step. 357 of 600 ally-capable personalities are level 2+, and the shipped 'Blue Allies' preset carries a level-2 Chiaotzu. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS.

#8 OPEN — Control of Combat never returns to the MP at the end of Combat. endCombatStep (combat.ts:174) calls only releaseControlIfMpRecovered, which refuses while mp.stageIndex <= 1 (turn.ts:120-122) — exactly the condition required to take control in the first place. An Ally that covered on turn 1 is still the fighter on turn 9, and the attacker side is never re-prompted.

#40 OPEN — 'raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage' heals whoever is in Control. abilities.ts:41 and :67 both resolve to the controller, and EffectTarget is only 'user'|'foe' so the MP-vs-controller subject cannot be expressed. ~46 cards, and they exist precisely for the MP-down-with-an-Ally-covering situation they get wrong. Compounds with #8: because the flag never clears, an Ally can hold control during the Non-Combat Step too.

#36 OPEN — overlaying an Ally pushes a second PersonalityInPlay instead of stacking a level (reducer.ts:151/158), sets it 3 above 0 instead of its new level's top stage, and rejects a level-2 Ally under a level-1 MP that CRD:554 explicitly permits.
bundles.whyItMatters: Ally decks are a mainstream archetype and #16 makes any Ally above level 1 self-destruct on the first Power-Up — it then sits at rating 0, so the PAT puts it in the bottom bracket forever and loseStages computes Math.min(n, 0) = 0, meaning redirected damage overflows entirely into life cards. Redirecting to an Ally, the main reason to field one, becomes strictly worse than eating the hit. #8 then quietly hands the wrong personality's rating to every subsequent physical attack.
bundles.unlocks: Allies become playable at all above level 1, and the MP/Ally distinction (ratings, healing, control) starts behaving as printed.
bundles.approach: #16 is a one-line clamp in currentRatings (index by `Math.min(currentLevel, levelCardIds.length) - 1`), which is a no-op for MPs and stays correct if #36's overlay later pushes onto levelCardIds — prefer it over setting currentLevel: 1, which forecloses overlay. #8 is an unconditional returnControlToMp called from endCombatStep, keeping the guarded release on the during-combat and Power-Up paths. #40 needs a `subject?: 'mp'` field on the two stage effects plus a data re-bake.

bundles.name: Non-Combat Step: timing and board legality
items: #17 OPEN — Non-Combat cards fire their effect the instant they are played and are spent immediately (noncombat.ts:94-113, inside the `step !== 'nonCombat'` guard), so all 88 non-Drill Non-Combat cards with an onPlay ability can never be held. 'A Burst of Energy' resolves before your own Power-Up Step; a starburst card can never be on the table to defend with, even though combat.ts:453 already accepts a defence from zone 'inPlay'. Note onplay.test.ts:126-156 actively locks the wrong behaviour in.

#18 OPEN — no Drill legality at all. playCard's only gate is the card-type check at noncombat.ts:62-64; isFreestyleDrill (drills.ts:33-37) has no production caller. Any mix of Styles and any number of duplicates go on the table simultaneously (159 Styled Drills). The refutation adds that styleOf reads only card.style, which is null for 9 Styled Drills, so even a Mastery deck's Tokui-Waza check misses them.

#19 OPEN — Locations/Battlegrounds are pushed unconditionally at noncombat.ts:79: no single-in-play rule, no removal of the incumbent from the game, no same-name check, and the opponent's is never displaced. 16 Locations + 17 Battlegrounds, all continuous and affecting both players.
bundles.whyItMatters: Drills are continuous and their effects stack, so #18 lets a player table every Drill they draw plus duplicates — and once bundle 4 makes Drill damage modifiers actually apply, an unrestricted Drill board becomes the dominant strategy rather than an inert one. #17 removes all timing control from a whole card class and makes the starburst defence unreachable.
bundles.unlocks: Drills and Locations become a real deckbuilding constraint rather than free accumulation; reactive Non-Combat cards become holdable, which is what CRD Attack Phase option 3 and defence option 2 are for.
bundles.approach: #19 and #18 are small and independent — do them first (a uniqueness scan across both players' inPlay before the push, and a drillStyleOf derived from title OR the style field, per the refutation's correction). #17 is the large one: split noncombat.ts:45-117 so playCard is pure entry-into-play, add a `useCard` action gated on the Attack Phase, and rewrite the five onplay.test.ts cases that assert immediate resolution.

bundles.name: Dragon Ball identity and the victory check
items: #20 OPEN — a 'set' is the printing's expansion saga and a ball's identity is its card NAME (victory.ts:49-50), with the same grouping duplicated in resolveCapture (combat.ts:879-887) and a third saga-based copy in decks.ts:176-183. Every shipped ball has number: null. Live consequences, all reproduced by two independent passes: 6 Alt. Dende balls + Earth Dragon Ball 3 (all saga 'Buu') is a FALSE WIN; a genuine Earth set split across the 'Unknown' and 'Saiyan' printings NEVER wins and never even defers on capture; and a CRD-legal Dende + Alt. Dende deck is rejected at deck build.

#46 OPEN — isDragonBall (damage.ts:36-40) trusts rules.type only, and tts-9f900382-12 'Upa, Littlefoot' is mistyped 'Dragon Ball' in the catalog. In a Life Deck it can never be discarded as damage and cycles forever, which reports unpayable damage and triggers a FALSE Survival loss at combat.ts:797-800; played, it counts as an eighth ball toward the win.

#45 OPEN — steps 14 and 15 run inverted: finishSuccessfulAttack (combat.ts:795, setting resolutionStep = 15 at :153) precedes the capture read at combat.ts:804. resolutionStep never takes the value 14, so the UI's sequence bar jumps 13 -> 15 and then raises a prompt for a step it says has passed. Live harm is ordering and display only until an effect can touch a ball.
bundles.whyItMatters: A player can win outright without a real set, and a player who legitimately collects seven balls across two printings can never win — and capture, the primary route, misses identically. Both outcomes are silent and unrecoverable. #46 can hand someone a Survival loss they did not earn. Frequency is lower than the combat bundles because it needs a ball deck, but when it fires it decides the game.
bundles.unlocks: A trustworthy win condition, one canonical ball-identity helper shared by victory, capture and deck validation (they currently disagree in three places), and the correct step-14 anchor for the capture routes in bundle 12.
bundles.approach: One shared ballIdentity(card) parsing the TITLE — strip a leading 'Alt. ', match /^(Earth|Namek|Dende) Dragon Ball ([1-7])$/i — returning family+index. Bucket victory.ts by family and key by index, delete the duplicated loop in resolveCapture and call the exported helper, map decks.ts:181 to family. Make isDragonBall require both the type and a parsable title, and fix the catalog mistype. Correction to the stale finding text: the copy-limit sliver it lists as broken is already fixed by the name|saga|level identity at decks.ts:142-147 — do not redo it. Existing fixtures (victory.test.ts:11-16, dragon-victory.test.ts:17-22) give balls a real number and a saga that IS the set, so they must be rebuilt from the real catalog or they will keep hiding this.

bundles.name: Deck construction legality
items: #35 OPEN — playAlly gates level only (reducer.ts:141-143). Alignment is copied at reducer.ts:150 and never compared, canBeAlly is loaded and read by no engine code, and personalityName is never compared to the MP's. A Hero Goku deck fields Nappa and a second Goku, in play and in deck validation. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS. Data caveat: canBeAlly is hardcoded true for all 600 personalities, so that clause needs curated data before it has teeth; alignment (326 Hero / 237 Villain / 37 Rogue) is usable today. Compare against p.alignment, not the current level card's — the shipped 'Blue Allies' MP mixes alignments across its level cards.

#27 PARTIAL — copy limits are counted per printing, not per title. decks.ts:142-147 keys on name|saga|level; dropping saga is a one-line fix. 205 non-Personality titles have 2+ printings, so 6 copies of a limit-3 card or 4 of a limit-1 Mastery are legal today. cheap-fixes.test.ts:160-175 currently asserts the wrong behaviour and must be inverted.

#42 OPEN — the deck-construction rule that an Ally must be 2 levels below the MP's highest printed level is enforced nowhere; only the weaker play-time rule (maxAllyLevel = mp.currentLevel) exists, and it loosens as the MP advances.

#43 OPEN — 31 catalog entries print 'Sensei Deck only' and nothing anywhere reads that phrase; they are accepted in the Life Deck. Sequence with #37 or gate it behind DeckValidationOptions, since until the Sensei Deck is materialised the check makes those cards unplayable rather than misplaced.

#41 OPEN — Saiyan/Namekian Tokui-Waza is granted on Mastery style alone (mastery.ts:48-83) with no Heritage check on the MP, and decks.ts:198 raises the deck ceiling to 90 the same way. That is +1 PUR all game (turn.ts:83) plus Endurance (damage.ts:149) for a deck not entitled to them.

#37 OPEN — the Sensei Deck never exists: deck.senseiDeck validates then evaporates (setup.ts:95-98 instantiates only the Sensei card itself), and there is no action, step or phase in which the setup-step-6 swap could happen. Large; split out.
bundles.whyItMatters: Everything here is decided once at deck build and then shapes every turn of the game. #27 in particular means a player draws a limit-3 combat card twice as often as the rules allow, all game, with no visible tell. #41's +1 PUR compounds directly with bundle 1's power-up fix.
bundles.unlocks: Decks that are actually legal, which is the precondition for any balance judgement about the other bundles. Note the alignment check will make the shipped 'Blue Allies' preset illegal (Villain MP, seven Hero Allies), so the presets need rebuilding alongside it.
bundles.approach: #27 and #42 are one-liners in decks.ts; #43 is a regex plus a loop over deck.life only (not the merged counts map). #35 is a few checks duplicated in reducer.ts and validateDeck. #41 wants the CRD:908-948 rosters transcribed into two frozen Sets in mastery.ts — smaller and safer than a data migration. Leave #37 for its own sitting.

bundles.name: Personality powers, Constant Combat Powers and the Prepare Phase
items: #12 OPEN — no personality card has an ability at all: enrich-tts.ts:471 explicitly skips ability parsing for type Personality, so 0 of 601 personalities carry abilities despite all 601 having rules.text. There is no action to invoke a power, no once-per-turn tracking on PersonalityInPlay, no reset on a level change, and no MP-vs-Ally exclusion. 'personalityPower' is a trigger produced and consumed by nothing.

#13 OPEN — Constant Combat Powers have no continuous layer. The 'constant' trigger (shared/abilities.ts:14) is read by no source file; 209 of 601 personalities print one. The CRD:495 rule that a constant power switches off while another personality holds Control is also unrepresented.

#28 OPEN — the Prepare Phase runs only the defender's draw (combat.ts:76-89). Neither player's 'When entering Combat' half exists, and the whenEnteringCombat trigger declared at shared/abilities.ts:13 is emitted by no parser branch and consumed by nothing. 149 cards print that text and do nothing all game. VERIFIED IN THIS PASS (grep confirms the trigger is dead).

Related: the Defense Shields printed on personalities (Android 18, Android 16, Vegeta Ascendant…) never fire at step 7, because activateDefenseShields (combat.ts:386-417) scans only zones.inPlay — CRD defence option 3 is unreachable.
bundles.whyItMatters: Every Main Personality and Ally in the game is currently a stat block with inert text, and one of the two legal ways to spend an Attack Phase (using a Personality Power to attack) does not exist. plan.recommendation:
Start with bundle 1 (the turn loop), and inside it do the power-up one-liner before anything else: setting `state.poweredUpThisTurn = true` alongside the automatic power-up at packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:92 is a single line that stops every personality in the game climbing at twice its printed rate, and every PAT lookup, every damage total and every attrition judgement downstream depends on the scouters being in the right place. Then do the Discard Step, because an unbounded hand is what currently makes the defence side of combat unfalsifiable — a defender always has a card, so no amount of work on bundles 2-4 will visibly change how a game plays until hands are trimmed. Declare and Rejuvenation complete the loop and are the cheapest way to make Locations, Battlegrounds and the whole skip-combat line real. Bundle 1 is the only bundle where every item fires every turn for both players, and it is the prerequisite for being able to tell whether anything else you fix actually worked.

Two deviations worth making deliberately rather than by accident. First, if this server is ever going to accept a connection from outside a fully trusted LAN, promote bundle 5 ahead of everything — it contains a one-message instant win (room.ts:280) and a one-message process kill (reducer.ts:166), both fixable in an afternoon. Second, regardless of ordering, pull the `answerPrompt` promptId check out of bundle 5 and do it with bundle 1: bundles 1-3 all add new prompts, and a double-clicked button silently eating the defender's Endurance decision is a bug two friends will actually hit and will not understand.

After bundle 1, work down 2 -> 3 -> 4 in order — declaration, defence, then damage arithmetic — because that is the order the battle sequence resolves in and each one makes the next observable. Do not start bundle 4's Drill modifiers before bundle 8's Drill legality is at least scoped: making 85 inert Drills live on an unrestricted board where a player can table every Drill they draw, in any mix of Styles, in triplicate, would swing the game further from the CRD than leaving them inert does today.

confirmedNewFindings.title: Declare Step is declared in STEPS but implemented nowhere — combat is mandatory
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: docs/CRD.txt:232-233 — "4) Declare Step: In this ste you declare if you are going to enter Combat with your opponent. If you choose not to declare Combat skip the Combat Step and go to the Discard Step." Also CRD.txt:2459 ("You're Invited") refers to "their Declare Step" as a real step.
confirmedNewFindings.defect: The string 'declare' appears in exactly two non-test places in the whole repo: packages/shared/src/state.ts:10 and its generated .d.ts. No engine file ever reads state.step === 'declare', there is no `declaredCombat` (or equivalent) field on GameState (packages/shared/src/state.ts:201-229 lists only skipCombatThisTurn and poweredUpThisTurn), and there is no action in the protocol to declare or decline combat (packages/shared/src/protocol.ts:13-31). advanceStep therefore walks declare -> combat unconditionally, and reducer.ts:93 immediately calls beginCombat. I verified this at runtime against the built engine: reducing {type:'advanceStep'} from step 'declare' yields step 'combat' with state.combat created and the defender's 3-card Prepare draw taken, with no decision point. The only way combat is ever skipped is the involuntary Location/Battleground path (turn.ts:59-64). combat.ts:18 admits this in its own header: "NOT modeled: Final Physical Attack, the Declare step".
confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: The attacker can never decline combat. Every turn that is not forced to skip by a Location becomes a combat turn, so the defender always draws 3 in the Prepare Phase, and the defensive/attrition line of play the CRD offers (skip combat, keep your hand, rejuvenate) does not exist. It also makes the Rejuvenation entitlement unreachable by choice, since that entitlement keys on not having declared combat.
confirmedNewFindings.confirmedBy: Confirmed against current code; every citation checks out. CRD.txt:232-233 reads verbatim as quoted (including the "ste" typo), and CRD.txt:211, :245, :248, :1750, :2459 all corroborate the Declare Step as a real decision point with downstream consequences. In the engine: packages/shared/src/state.ts:10 declares 'declare' in STEPS, and a Grep of the literal 'declare' across packages/*/src returns only that line plus one test (packages/engine/src/turn-integrity.test.ts:125) — no production code reads state.step === 'declare'. packages/engine/src/turn.ts:48 computes `const next: Step = STEPS[(i + 1) % STEPS.length]!` and line 65 assigns `state.step = next` unconditionally; the sole bypass is turn.ts:59 `if (next === 'combat' && state.skipCombatThisTurn)`, and skipCombatThisTurn is written in exactly one place, packages/engine/src/noncombat.ts:83 (Location/Battleground), i.e. the involuntary path only. packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:93 then fires `beginCombat(state, db, events)`, and beginCombat (packages/engine/src/combat.ts:76-89) calls `draw(state, defender, PREPARE_DRAW)` unconditionally before creating state.combat. GameState (packages/shared/src/state.ts:202-231) has no declaredCombat-equivalent — only skipCombatThisTurn (:217) and poweredUpThisTurn (:220). The Action union (packages/shared/src/protocol.ts:9-31) has no declare/decline-combat member, and 'pass' cannot substitute because passPhase returns 'not in combat' when state.combat is absent — and by the time combat exists the defender has already taken the 3-card Prepare draw. The client offers only a blanket advanceStep (packages/client/src/App.tsx:113). combat.ts:18 itself still lists "the Declare step" as NOT modeled. Minor imprecisions that do not affect the defect: the claim gives GameState as state.ts:201-229 (actually 202-231), and the Rejuvenation entitlement is in fact absent altogether rather than merely unreachable — `rejuvenate` exists only as a card effect (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:151) and reducer.ts's advanceStep case has no 'rejuvenation' branch, so the claim understates rather than overstates. Not refutable as a duplicate-of-accepted-gap either: README.md:60-78's deliberate-gaps list does not include the Declare Step. It does duplicate rank 6 of the repo's committed finding register data/crd-audit.json:76-88, but that file is a snapshot of open findings (its rank 1 and rank 5 have since been fixed in code), not a list of accepted limitations, and this gap remains open.

confirmedNewFindings.title: Discard Step is a pass-through: neither player's hand is trimmed to 1 card
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: docs/CRD.txt:240-241 — "6) Discard Step: If you are the attacker and you have more than 1 card in your hand during this step, place all but 1 of your cards into the discard pile... you may have no more than 1 card in your hand at the end of this step. Your opponent does the same, right after you discard." Corroborated by CRD.txt:2230 (Saiyan Truce Card), which exists solely to exempt a player from this discard.
confirmedNewFindings.defect: Nothing anywhere implements the hand-size rule. A repo-wide grep for hand limit / HAND_LIMIT / 'all but 1' / hand.length > / maxHand / handSize across packages/engine/src, packages/shared/src and packages/server/src returns zero hits. The only step checks that exist in non-test engine/server code are noncombat.ts:55, reducer.ts:86/91/92/93/105/134, turn.ts:60/65 and victory.ts:94 — none of them names 'discard'. discardFromHand (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:165) is only ever called from card effects (abilities.ts:133, abilities.ts:219), never from the turn machinery. Verified at runtime: with P0 holding 7 cards and P1 holding 6, advancing out of step 'discard' leaves both hands at 7 and 6 and both discard piles at 0.
confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: Hands grow without bound. The attacker draws 3 each Draw Step (turn.ts:22) and the defender draws 3 more in every Prepare Phase (combat.ts:56, combat.ts:80), and none of it is ever given back. Card advantage, hand-size pressure and the whole reason to spend cards in combat are removed, and every card that manipulates the Discard Step (Saiyan Truce Card, Black Weakness Drill) has nothing to act on.
confirmedNewFindings.confirmedBy: Claim stands; I could not refute it. (1) CRD text is exactly as quoted at docs/CRD.txt:240-241 ("If you are the attacker and you have more than 1 card in your hand during this step, place all but 1 of your cards into the discard pile... Your opponent does the same, right after you discard."), corroborated by docs/CRD.txt:2230 (Saiyan Truce Card, which exists to exempt its user from this discard and names Black Weakness Drill). (3) Repo-wide grep of packages/engine/src, packages/shared/src, packages/server/src for hand limit / HAND_LIMIT / "all but 1" / hand.length / maxHand / handSize / MAX_HAND yields only test assertions and unrelated String.trim() hits; the only non-test 'discard' step references are turn.ts:60 and turn.ts:62 (the skip-combat jump target) and a comment at reducer.ts:83. No Discard-Step prompt exists either — the five newPrompt sites in combat.ts (300, 317, 728, 777, 806) are controlOfCombat, defend, redirect, endurance and capture. confirmedNewFindings.title: Rejuvenation Step is a pass-through: the top discard card is never returned to the Life Deck
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: docs/CRD.txt:244-248 — "7) Rejuvenation Step: If you are the attacker and you did not declare Combat in the Declare Step, you may take the top card of your discard pile and place it facedown at the bottom of your Life Deck... The Rejuvenation Step itself is not optional, and you must go through the Rejuvenation Step during each of your turns." Also CRD.txt:2041 — "You may only put the top card back into your Life Deck during your Rejuvenation Step and not during your opponent's."
confirmedNewFindings.defect: reducer.ts:91-93 special-cases only 'draw', 'powerUp' and 'combat' on entering a step; entering or leaving 'rejuvenation' runs no code at all, and no engine file tests state.step === 'rejuvenation'. The rejuvenate() helper exists (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:151-161) and is well tested, but it is reachable only as a card effect (abilities.ts:129-130, abilities.ts:212-213) — never from the step of the same name. Verified at runtime: with a 5-card discard pile and a 30-card Life Deck, advancing out of step 'rejuvenation' leaves the pile at 5 and the deck at 30 and moves straight to the next player's Draw Step.
confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: Skipping combat costs a player a turn and buys them nothing, so the only defensive/recycling engine in the game is dead. Combined with the missing Declare Step, a deck that intends to skip combat to rebuild its Life Deck simply cannot function, and Survival-loss timing is accelerated for everyone because no card ever comes back.
confirmedNewFindings.confirmedBy: Confirmed against current code. CRD quotes are verbatim and correctly cited: docs/CRD.txt:244 ("7) Rejuvenation Step"), :245 (the "you may take the top card of your discard pile and place it facedown at the bottom of your Life Deck" rule, conditioned on not declaring Combat), :248 ("The Rejuvenation Step itself is not optional..."), and :2041 ("You may only put the top card back into your Life Deck during your Rejuvenation Step and not during your opponent's."). confirmedNewFindings.title: Power-Up Step applies twice: the automatic power-up does not set poweredUpThisTurn
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: docs/CRD.txt:229 — "If you are the attacker, yout Main Personality powers up by moving his Scouter up a number of power stages equal to his Power Up Rating (PUR)... All of your Allies also power up in this step, but only by 1 power stage regardless of any Ally's PUR." One power-up per Power-Up Step.
confirmedNewFindings.defect: Entering the Power-Up Step auto-powers-up (reducer.ts:92: `else if (state.step === 'powerUp') powerUp(state, state.activePlayerIdx, db, events);`) but never sets state.poweredUpThisTurn. The flag is only ever written at reducer.ts:113 and cleared at turn.ts:55 (grep for poweredUpThisTurn returns exactly those three sites plus the type declaration at packages/shared/src/state.ts:220). Allies are double-powered the same way (turn.ts:137).
confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: Any client that sends the powerUp action after advancing into the step (the natural thing to do, since the action exists and reports no error) gives its MP double PUR and every Ally 2 stages instead of 1 every turn. Personalities sit far higher on the ladder than the rules allow, which inflates PAT lookups and blunts power-stage attrition — the exact failure the guard's own comment at reducer.ts:100-104 was written to prevent.
confirmedNewFindings.confirmedBy: Confirmed real, by code inspection and runtime reproduction. packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:92 auto-powers-up on entering the Power-Up Step (`else if (state.step === 'powerUp') powerUp(state, state.activePlayerIdx, db, events);`) without setting state.poweredUpThisTurn, and packages/engine/src/turn.ts:133-141 (powerUp itself) does not set it either. confirmedNewFindings.title: Prepare Phase runs only the defender's draw; "When entering Combat" effects never fire for either player
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: docs/CRD.txt:260-270 — "The Attacker's Half of the Prepare Phase. As the Attacker, you prepare for the fight by using all your effects that happen 'When entering Combat.'... The Defender's Half of the Prepare Phase. The Defender now does these 2 things in this order. 1. Use any 'When entering Combat' effects on his cards in play... 2. Draw 3 cards from the top of his Life Deck." Real cards depend on it: CRD.txt:1338 (Android 18 Lv.1), CRD.txt:1431 (Blue Deceiving Drill), CRD.txt:1786 (King Cold Lv.1).
confirmedNewFindings.defect: beginCombat performs the defender's 3-card draw and sets up combat state, and nothing else — neither half of the Prepare Phase's "When entering Combat" effects is offered or applied. The trigger is declared in the ability model (packages/shared/src/abilities.ts:13, 'whenEnteringCombat') but the identifier appears in no other source file in the repo: no parser branch emits it and no engine code consumes it (grep across packages/engine/src, packages/server/src and packages/client/src returns nothing; only packages/shared/src/abilities.ts and its generated .d.ts match). This is a sub-phase of the Combat Step rather than a top-level STEPS entry, so it is adjacent to the step audit rather than part of it.

Coverage is partial, so those are the tabletop-assist fallback for effects the engine can't resolve yet." That is a known-tracked, deliberate design decision; the claim itself concedes it. - packages/server/src/index.ts:123 does `JSON.parse(raw) as ClientMessage` (a cast, no runtime validation); index.ts:145-147 validates only `typeof action.type !== 'string'`.
- packages/server/src/room.ts:278-282 authorize() never inspects stageIndex.
- packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:117 forwards it untouched.

- combat.ts:267 computeBaseDamage(attCtl.currentRating, defCtl.currentRating) receives undefined; pat.ts:104 `table.damage[ai]?.[di] ?? 0` falls through to 0, so attacks silently deal zero.
- combat.ts:297 and combat.ts:956 test `stageIndex > MP_DOWN_STAGES`; NaN > 1 is false, so the MP reads as permanently at its bottom 2 power stages and an Ally can always take Control of Combat.
- turn.ts:100 moveStage (NaN + delta) and combat.ts:103 (from - taken) both propagate NaN forever, so power-ups and combat damage never restore a sane index.

confirmedNewFindings.title: Sequential card uids survive redaction and leak Life Deck composition

confirmedNewFindings.title: A level-2+ Ally's power rating collapses to 0 on the first recompute (levelCardIds vs currentLevel mismatch)
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: docs/CRD.txt:544 "When you place Allies into play, they must be the same personality level as your Main Personality or lower... If your Main Personality is level 2, you can play level 1 or level 2 allies."; :561 "Allies always Power-Up by 1 during your Power-Up Step"; :583 "You also use the Ally's power rating when the Physical Attack Table is used."
confirmedNewFindings.defect: playAlly builds the PersonalityInPlay with `levelCardIds: [inst.cardId]` (one entry) but `currentLevel: per.level`. Every later lookup goes through `currentRatings()` in turn.ts:88, which reads `p.levelCardIds[p.currentLevel - 1]`. For a level-2 Ally that index is 1 -> undefined -> the function falls back to `[0]`. The `currentRating` cached at creation (correct, taken straight from `per.powerRatings`) is therefore immediately stale relative to everything the engine computes afterwards. Verified with Android 13 Lv2 as an Ally under a level-2 MP: enters at stageIndex 3 / currentRating 1930000; the very next Power-Up Step runs moveStage, which clamps to `ratings.length - 1 = 0`, leaving stageIndex 0 / currentRating 0. A level-1 Ally in the same harness correctly goes stage 3 -> 4 (rating 699000 -> 999000). 357 of the 600 ally-capable personality cards in data/cards.tts.enriched.json are level 2 or higher.
confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: Any Ally above level 1 is destroyed the moment anything touches its stages. It sits at rating 0 forever, so the PAT always puts it in the bottom bracket (max damage taken, min damage dealt); loseStages computes `Math.min(n, 0) = 0`, so it can never lose power stages and every point of physical damage redirected to it overflows into life cards instead. Redirecting damage to an Ally — the main reason to field one — becomes strictly worse than taking it on the MP.
confirmedNewFindings.confirmedBy:
CONFIRMED — the defect is real in the current code, and I reproduced it end-to-end.

Code, verbatim:
- packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:151-152 builds the Ally with `levelCardIds: [inst.cardId],` / `currentLevel: per.level,` — a one-element array paired with the card's own personality level.
- packages/engine/src/turn.ts:87-90: `export function currentRatings(p, db) { const cardId = p.levelCardIds[p.currentLevel - 1]; return (cardId ? db.personality(cardId)?.powerRatings : undefined) ?? [0]; }` — no `isAlly` branch, so a level-2 Ally indexes `[1]` of a length-1 array -> undefined -> falls back to `[0]`.

Reproduction (harness against packages/engine/dist, MP level 2, both allies with ladder [0,1000,2000,3000,4000,5000] / [0,100,...,500]):
- L1 ally: on play levelCardIds=["a1"] currentLevel=1 stage=3 rating=300; currentRatings = [0,100,200,300,400,500]; after Power-Up stage=4 rating=400. Correct.
- L2 ally: on play levelCardIds=["a2"] currentLevel=2 stage=3 rating=3000 (cached value correct); currentRatings = [0]; after Power-Up stage=0 rating=0; `syncRating` alone also drops rating to 0.
The `playAlly` action returned no error for the level-2 Ally — the legality gate (maxAllyLevel, packages/engine/src/noncombat.ts:123, MP currentLevel 2) correctly permits it, so this is reached on legal play, not an edge case.

Downstream impact confirmed in code:
- packages/engine/src/turn.ts:97-104 `moveStage` clamps to `ratings.length - 1` = 0, which is what collapses the stage on the very first Power-Up (turn.ts:137 `for (const ally of p.allies) moveStage(state, ally, 1, db, events);`).
- packages/engine/src/combat.ts:267 feeds `defCtl.currentRating` / `attCtl.currentRating` straight into `computeBaseDamage` (packages/engine/src/pat.ts:96-105), so rating 0 lands in the bottom PAT bracket.
- packages/engine/src/combat.ts:100-109 `loseStages` uses `const taken = Math.min(n, from);` — with `from === 0` the Ally absorbs zero stages and `combat.ts:556-558` overflows the entire hit into life cards, so redirecting to the Ally is strictly worse than eating it on the MP.

CRD evidence is accurate at the cited lines: docs/CRD.txt:544 ("If your Main Personality is level 2, you can play level 1 or level 2 allies."), :561 (Allies always Power-Up by 1), :583 (the Ally's power rating is used on the Physical Attack Table).

Not a duplicate of a tracked gap: docs/RULES-NOTES.md:83-95 documents the Ally rules as intended behaviour and records no known level-indexing gap.

Not covered by tests: every ally fixture in the suite uses `currentLevel: 1` with a single levelCardId (packages/engine/src/control-of-combat.test.ts:39-44, battle-sequence.test.ts:61-66, combat-reentry.test.ts:102-107), and the only playAlly happy-path test (packages/engine/src/cheap-fixes.test.ts:211-215) uses the level-1 'ally1' card (defined at cheap-fixes.test.ts:53). The reachability figure in the claim also checks out: data/cards.tts.enriched.json has 600 personality cards with canBeAlly, 357 of them level 2 or higher, and packages/engine/src/decks.ts imposes no ally-level restriction on life-deck contents.

One caveat I could not settle: `PersonalityInPlay.currentLevel` (packages/shared/src/state.ts:50-51) is used by the MP path (turn.ts:79 purOf, turn.ts:163-167 advanceLevel, victory.ts:127) as an index into the MP's level ladder, so the correct fix — set the Ally's `currentLevel` to 1 (its levelCardIds ladder has one entry) or make `currentRatings` short-circuit on `isAlly` — depends on whether any Ally-facing rule needs to read the Ally's printed level after it is in play. I did not find such a reader (`maxAllyLevel` reads `mp.currentLevel`, not the Ally's), but I did not exhaustively audit packages/server/src or packages/client for consumers of an Ally's `currentLevel`.

confirmedNewFindings.title: answerPrompt ignores action.promptId, so a stale or duplicated answer resolves whatever prompt is open now

confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: A double-clicked button, a client retry, or a reconnect replay silently spends the defender's Endurance card and forfeits the damage prevention — which per CRD ~L1147 can also be what stops a Dragon Ball capture. The player sees a decision they never made.

One correction to the claim's impact wording: the client does not resend pending actions on reconnect (the WebSocket effect in useGame.ts:106-160 runs once with no pending replay), so 'reconnect replay' is not a live vector in the reference client; a duplicate send (double-click before re-render, a retry, or any non-reference client) is. confirmedNewFindings.title: moveCard does not validate toZone or toPlayerIdx and throws an uncaught TypeError that kills the server process
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: No CRD rule bears on this — it is a robustness defect. The legal zone set is the ZONES tuple in packages/shared/src/state.ts:18-25; the CRD's zones (Life Deck, hand, discard, in play, removed from game, Sensei Deck) are what that tuple encodes.
confirmedNewFindings.defect: `state.players[action.toPlayerIdx ?? loc.playerIdx]!.zones[action.toZone].push(inst)` trusts both fields. `toZone` is typed `Zone` and `toPlayerIdx` `number`, but the action arrives as raw JSON off a socket — packages/server/src/index.ts:152 checks only `typeof action.type === 'string'`, and authorize() in packages/server/src/room.ts:279 lets moveCard through because it carries no `playerIdx`. Verified against the engine: toZone 'bogusZone' throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')"; toZone '__proto__' or 'constructor' throws "...push is not a function"; toPlayerIdx 5 throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'zones')". Verified against a real Room: `room.handleAction('c0', {type:'moveCard', cardUid, toZone:'nope'})` throws straight out of handleAction (room.ts:179 calls reduce with no try/catch), and packages/server/src/index.ts:120-161 has no catch around `conn.room.handleAction` — its only try/catch is around JSON.parse at :122. There is no process-level uncaughtException handler anywhere in packages/server/src.
confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: Any seated player can crash the whole server with one four-field message, ending every game in every room in that process, not just their own. The card itself is not duplicated or lost — reduce mutates a structuredClone and the room never assigns the result — so the damage is availability, not state.
confirmedNewFindings.confirmedBy:
CONFIRMED — I read the current code and reproduced the crash; nothing in the claim is stale.

1. The cited line is verbatim present. packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:162-168:
   case 'moveCard': {
     const loc = findInstance(state, action.cardUid);
     if (!loc) return fail(prev, 'card not found');
     const inst = state.players[loc.playerIdx]!.zones[loc.zone].splice(loc.idx, 1)[0]!;
     state.players[action.toPlayerIdx ?? loc.playerIdx]!.zones[action.toZone].push(inst);
     break;
   }
   `toZone` and `toPlayerIdx` are used with zero validation. The only guard in the whole case is the `!loc` card-not-found check. Contrast the neighbouring `playAlly` case (reducer.ts:125-127), which does `const p = state.players[action.playerIdx]; if (!p) return fail(...)` — so the defensive pattern exists in this same switch and was simply not applied here.

2. The legal-zone set is packages/shared/src/state.ts:18-25 (ZONES = lifeDeck, hand, discard, inPlay, removed, sensei), and `Zone` is a compile-time-only type — there is no runtime membership check anywhere. Confirmed there is no runtime validator for Action shapes: packages/shared/src/protocol.ts:9-31 is a pure type union, and `moveCard` is declared at protocol.ts:20 as `{ type: 'moveCard'; cardUid: string; toZone: Zone; toPlayerIdx?: number }`.

3. Reproduced empirically against the compiled engine (packages/engine/dist/reducer.js:154, same expression). I built a two-player state with one card in hand and called reduce(state, action, db, 0):
   - toZone 'discard'  -> no throw, error undefined (baseline works)
   - toZone 'bogusZone' -> THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
   - toZone '__proto__' -> THREW TypeError: ...zones[action.toZone].push is not a function
   - toZone 'constructor' -> THREW TypeError: ...push is not a function
   - toPlayerIdx 5 -> THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'zones')
   - toZone omitted entirely -> THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
   All five failure modes the claim asserts are real.

4. The path from a socket to that line is unguarded end to end:
   - packages/server/src/index.ts:149-156 (`case 'action'`) validates only `if (!action || typeof action.type !== 'string')` at :152, then calls `conn.room.handleAction(conn.id, action)` at :155 with no try/catch. The only try/catch in handleMessage is at :122 around JSON.parse.
   - packages/server/src/room.ts:176-179: `authorize(action, seatIdx, this.state!)` then `reduce(...)`. handleAction (154-183) has no try/catch.
   - authorize (room.ts:278-283) rejects only when the action carries a numeric `playerIdx` that differs from the seat, plus an advanceStep turn check. `moveCard` carries no `playerIdx`, so it passes through untouched. This is deliberate per the doc comment at room.ts:274-277 ("Deliberately *not* blocked: uid-targeted manual adjustments (`setStage`, `setAnger`, `moveCard`)"), but that comment is about letting a player touch an *opponent's* card — it is not a decision to accept an out-of-range zone name, and it is why `moveCard` is uniquely unguarded where `drawCards`/`powerUp`/`playAlly` are protected by the playerIdx check.

5. The process-death consequence is real, not speculative. I confirmed with a standalone probe using this repo's own `ws` (node_modules/ws) that a synchronous throw from a `ws.on('message')` listener propagates through Receiver._write -> writeOrBuffer and terminates the process (exit code 1, stack through ws/lib/websocket.js:1239). packages/server/src/index.ts:71 registers exactly that shape: `ws.on('message', (raw) => handleMessage(ws, conn, hub, String(raw)))`. The `ws.on('error', ...)` at :73 does not catch listener throws. A repo-wide grep for `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` across packages/ (excluding node_modules and dist) returned nothing, so there is no process-level net.

6. Not a duplicate of a tracked gap: no test file in packages/ mentions `moveCard` (grep over *.test.ts returned nothing), and docs/RULES-NOTES.md contains no TODO/known-gap entry for it.

Scope caveat, stated precisely: the attacker must be a seated (non-spectator) client in a *started* room — room.ts:161 rejects spectators and :163-172 rejects non-lobby actions before the game starts. Within that scope the claim holds exactly as written, including the impact analysis: reduce clones via structuredClone (reducer.ts:27, :71) and room.ts:181 never runs after the throw, so game state is untouched and the damage is availability of the whole process, not corruption.

Only correction: authorize() is declared at room.ts:278, not :279. That is a one-line offset in a supporting citation; the primary engineLocation (reducer.ts:166) is exact.

confirmedNewFindings.title: Empower is fully implemented in the engine but no client can ever declare it
confirmedNewFindings.crdEvidence: CRD.txt:1102 — "Empower always appears as "Empower X"... When you perform an attack with Empower, after you pay any costs for the attack, you may declare to use the Empower. If you do, the attack will do +X life cards"; CRD.txt:319 (battle-sequence step 2) — "the attacker pays costs... and announces if he is using any Empower effect on the card to boost its damage."
confirmedNewFindings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:180-181 (action case), packages/engine/src/combat.ts:355-361 (declareEmpower), packages/engine/src/combat.ts:560 and combat.ts:714 (readers of atk.empower)
confirmedNewFindings.defect: `declareEmpower` is the only writer of `AttackInProgress.empower` (shared/src/state.ts:108). confirmedNewFindings.playerImpact: No attack in any game can ever be Empowered. Every card printing "Empower X" plays as if the keyword were absent, so a whole damage-boost mechanic — and the trade-off of deleting the card's later text to use it — is silently unavailable to both players.
